Description
​​Centralized monitoring is an integral part of a risk-based monitoring strategy, defined as the timely, remote review of accumulating subject and operational data to help distinguish between reliable and unreliable data, trends, outliers, and unusual variability using analytics and statistical methods.
The central monitor is responsible for conducting a holistic and centralized statistical review of study data from study start through to study database lock according to the centralized monitoring plan, using analytical tools to identify emerging and existing risks to critical study data and process. The central monitor enables proactive identification, communication, escalation and management of risks at the study/country/site level. ​
RESPONSIBILITIES

• ​​Follow established procedures for the review of clinical trial data (Operational and Subject data) using a variety of tools and systems in alignment with the centralized monitoring plan and with support from the senior team members.

• ​Identify data quality trends indicative of systematic errors and potential performance issues at study/country/site and track the evidence of issues and potential risks with support from senior team members.

• ​Ensure results of reviews are appropriately documented per procedures.

• ​Support Central Monitoring teams with performance of assigned reviews with high quality, on-time results.

• ​Provide input to senior team member as needed to support development of risk characterization and reporting.

• ​Support review set-up as directed by assigned lead including updating department database, pulling reports, etc. as assigned.

• ​Share the responsibility for data quality at the study, country and site levels.​

Requirements
Education

• ​​Bachelor’s degree in a field relevant to clinical research.
Experience

• ​Minimum of 1 year of experience in central statistical monitoring with overall 6 years of experience in two or more operational areas such as clinical monitoring, data management, drug safety, medical monitoring, biometrics, or project management.

• ​Basic understanding of statistical monitoring and Risk Based Quality Management (RBQM) and their impact on data integrity.

• ​Thorough understanding of the processes associated with clinical study management, data management, and regulatory operations.

• ​Knowledge of clinical trial database systems (EDC, IRT, CTMS, etc.).

• ​Good computer skills, with knowledge of advanced MS Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) and the ability to learn and use interactive computer systems and tools.

• ​Ideally a basic level of understanding of descriptive analysis e.g. means, medians, significance, confidence intervals.

• ​Must have been involved in the analysis and review of clinical data, ability to extract pertinent information from standard study documentation, such as protocols, electronic study data systems with the ability to learn to identify trending of site/study data.

• ​Must be able to work in non-traditional work environments.

Attributes

• Fluent in English (excellent oral and written).

• Must be able to communicate clearly and effectively at all levels in an organization and with external customers.

• Must be a fast learner and able to understand new concepts quickly.

• Prioritization skills with ability to plan, monitor and manage workload fluidly in response to changing project demands.

• Satisfactory understanding of project protocol, project documentation including centralized monitoring and risk-based monitoring.

• Broad working knowledge of the roles, functions and process of conducting clinical trials.

• Must be able to manage time effectively, working with multiple functions and requirements.

• Must have been involved in the use of trial management or data management systems.

• Good knowledge of good clinical practices, and applicable Health Canada and Food and Drug Administration (FDA) regulations/guidelines.

(This job is only available in german)
Worum es geht
SIMON ist die Außendienst-Plattform für alle, die beim Kunden vor Ort arbeiten. Das reicht von der Pharmareferentin in der Apotheke über den Merchandiser im Lebensmittelmarkt bis zum Techniker im Heizungskeller. SIMON setzt auf die vorhandenen ERP- und CRM-Systeme auf und ist technisch in vier bis sechs Wochen startklar. Seit über zehn Jahren arbeiten anspruchsvolle Außendienstteams im Pharmabereich damit.
Jetzt bringen wir SIMON zu weiteren mittelständischen Herstellern, vor allem im Handel und FMCG sowie im technischen Kundendienst. Dafür suchen wir dich: jemanden, der die richtigen Leute findet, anspricht und vom ersten Kontakt bis zum produktiven Einsatz begleitet.
Wie wir verkaufen
Wir verkaufen SIMON so, wie man einen neuen Kollegen einstellt. Zuerst kommt das Kennenlernen: Der Interessent probiert einen Prototyp für seine Branche selbst aus. Darauf folgt das Vorstellungsgespräch, eine Demo mit einem Klickdummy in seinen eigenen Begriffen. Danach kommt die Probearbeit, ein Pilot mit fünf bis zehn Nutzern und vorab vereinbarten Erfolgskriterien. Erst dann folgt die Festanstellung, also Vertrag und Rollout. Nach drei Monaten gibt es ein Mitarbeitergespräch mit echten Zahlen.
Wir versprechen dabei nichts, was nicht stimmt. In jeder Demo sagen wir klar, was Standard ist, was konfiguriert und was entwickelt werden muss.
Deine Aufgaben

• Du identifizierst passende mittelständische Hersteller mit eigenem Außendienst und findest dort die richtigen Ansprechpartner, vor allem über LinkedIn und den Sales Navigator.

• Du sprichst Vertriebs- und Serviceleitungen persönlich an, über LinkedIn und am Telefon, und gewinnst sie für ein erstes Gespräch.

• Du baust dein LinkedIn-Profil zu einer erkennbaren fachlichen Stimme für Außendienstthemen aus.

• Du qualifizierst eingehende Anfragen von der Website und aus unseren Branchenprototypen.

• Du führst Demos und stimmst dafür kundenspezifische Prototypen mit unserem Produktteam ab.

• Du begleitest Interessenten durch ihre Entscheidung und bindest dabei Fachbereich, IT, Geschäftsführung, Datenschutz und Betriebsrat ein.

• Du verhandelst Pilotprojekte und Verträge.

• Du bleibst nach dem Vertrag Ansprechpartner für deine Kunden, gemeinsam mit unserem Beratungsteam, und entwickelst die Zusammenarbeit weiter.

Was du mitbringst

• Du hast mindestens drei Jahre Erfahrung im B2B-Vertrieb, idealerweise mit Software oder erklärungsbedürftigen Lösungen für den Mittelstand.

• Du hast nachweislich selbst Kunden gewonnen. LinkedIn-Direktansprache und Telefonakquise sind für dich Handwerk.

• Du schreibst Nachrichten, die nach Mensch klingen, und führst am Telefon ein Gespräch statt eines Skripts.

• Du hast Erfahrung mit Entscheidungen über mehrere Monate und mehrere Beteiligte, zum Beispiel mit IT-Abteilungen und Betriebsräten.

• Du sprichst Deutsch auf Muttersprachniveau. Englisch ist ein Plus.

• Ein großer Vorteil wäre eigene Erfahrung im Außendienst, im Handel oder im technischen Service.

Was du bekommst

• Gehalt mit Erfolgsbeteiligung: Gute Leistung zahlt sich bei uns aus, auch jenseits der Führungsebene. Wir vergüten nicht nur Abschlüsse, sondern auch qualifizierte Demo-Termine und Erweiterungen bei Bestandskunden.

• Werkzeuge, die verkaufen helfen: Prototypen, die Interessenten selbst ausprobieren, ein Produktteam, das kundenspezifische Klickdummys in wenigen Tagen baut, LinkedIn Sales Navigator und Zeit für den Aufbau deines Profils.

• Karriere und Weiterbildung: DMG Academy, Mentoring und Zugriff auf Lernplattformen zu KI, Kundenportalen und mehr.

• Agiles Arbeiten: Feedback, Mitgestaltung und Verantwortung statt Micromanagement. Du hast kurze Wege zu Geschäftsführung, Produkt und Beratung und echten Einfluss darauf, wie wir in neue Branchen gehen.

• Arbeitsmodelle nach Maß: Vollzeit, Teilzeit oder remote, mit nur zwei Stunden Kernzeit.

Job Title: MVA Lead Generation Senior Media Buyer

I want to hire you… and pay you a lot of money.

But this role isn't for most media buyers.

If you’re a senior media buyer based in the U.S. who is already actively managing accounts spending 7 figures per month on Meta and/or Google , keep reading.

Because if you're genuinely elite at media buying, obsessed with performance, and want to operate at a scale where small improvements can have massive impact, this could be the opportunity you're looking for.

We operate at serious scale.

You'll be working across 7-figure monthly advertising budgets , multiple platforms, multiple states and markets, and a creative operation capable of producing and testing a massive volume of new ads.

We don't need someone to simply maintain what we've built.

We want someone who can help us make it significantly better.

The Role

This is not a traditional media buyer role.

We don't need someone who waits for instructions, adjusts budgets, turns off bad ads, and calls it media buying.

And we definitely don't need someone who requires leadership to constantly tell them where the next opportunity is.

We're looking for someone who can take real ownership over performance.

Someone who can look across Meta, Google, states, campaigns, and hundreds of creatives and quickly determine:

• Where should we spend more?

• Where should we spend less?

• What's starting to work that we haven't fully capitalized on yet?

• Why is this state underperforming?

• What winning ads haven't we expanded yet?

• What creative are we missing?

• What should we test next?

Then actually execute.

You won't just optimize campaigns.

You'll help determine where the next level of growth comes from.

What You’ll Actually Own

1. Performance & Scaling

• You’ll help manage and optimize high-spend campaigns across Meta and Google , including YouTube, Search, and Performance Max.

• You'll continuously look across platforms and states to identify:

• Scaling opportunities

• Budget reallocation opportunities

• Performance inefficiencies

• Underperforming markets

• Testing gaps

You'll know our best-performing ads.

You'll know which concepts are starting to gain traction.

And you'll make sure we capitalize on them.

“This is working here → why aren't we running it here, here, and here?”

“This angle is crushing on Meta → let's test it on YouTube.”

“This state-specific concept is working → let's build it for every relevant market.”

“We're relying too heavily on UGC here → let's expand our creative diversity.”

“This angle is starting to work → creative team needs to build 10 more variations before everyone else catches it.”

You’ll bridge the gap between performance data and the creative team.

The creative team should always know what’s working, what’s starting to work, what’s getting fatigued, and what we need more of.

"Performance is bad."

Your job is to figure out why.

Then build and execute a plan to improve it.

This is your chance to be part of something outstandingly innovative!

title: Product Marketing Manager
description:
About Improvado

Improvado is a marketing data and AI analytics platform for enterprise brands and agencies. We connect 500+ marketing and sales data sources, normalize them through a governed data model, and put an AI agent on top so marketing teams can ask questions of their own data without going through BI or IT.
What we sell: extraction and 500+ connectors; data transformation (SQL and dbt-compatible); Marketing Data Governance - taxonomy, naming, data-quality rules; warehouse and storage; dashboards; AI agent and MCP access to live marketing data; DECS, data engineering as a service on a 2 to 4 week SLA.
Who buys it:

•
Economic buyers: CMO, VP Marketing, VP Demand Gen, agency COO and ops leadership

•
Technical evaluators: VP or Director of Marketing Analytics, marketing analysts, data engineering, sometimes IT and security

•
Segments: enterprise brands, mid-market, agencies

•
Verticals: pharma and healthcare, financial services, retail and eCommerce, gaming, agencies

Why this role, now

•
Our messaging is not aligned. Positioning, web, sales pitch, product and content each carry a different version of what Improvado is. The market categorizes us as "marketing ETL" while we position as an AI marketing analytics platform. That gap costs us deal quality and price.

•
The category is crowded and moving fast. Battlecards exist but decay, and nobody owns keeping them true.

•
Attribution, incrementality and causal measurement is where deals are won and lost - and it is the hardest thing to argue credibly without hand-waving.

•
Analyst firms are a silent blocker. When an enterprise buyer asks Gartner or Forrester about Improvado , there is no briefed narrative waiting for them.

You would not start from a blank page. We already have a positioning registry, roughly 11 documented buyer personas, a pain-point and value-prop library, competitor intel reports and about 10 battlecards. They are inconsistent and under-used. Your first job is to make one version true and make people use it.
What you'll own

•
Positioning and messaging. Core positioning, category framing and message hierarchy across ICPs and personas. ICP and persona documentation that is used, not filed. The messaging layer of new product and feature launches, including the internal rollout that makes the field able to sell it.

•
Competitive intelligence and win/loss. A structured win/loss interview program with quarterly readouts. Living battlecards. Monitoring competitor positioning, pricing and product moves, and driving our counter-positioning.

•
Sales enablement. The core pitch narrative, demo storyline and objection-handling framework. The messaging components of new-rep onboarding. A standing weekly cadence with Sales leadership - not quarterly check-ins. Direct support on competitive and enterprise deals: RFPs, security and technical evaluations, displacement plays.

•
Market and analyst relations. The Improvado narrative for Gartner, Forrester and category influencers, so that a buyer's analyst call becomes an accelerator rather than a blocker. Feeding structured market and buyer insight back into product prioritization.

What we're looking for

• 4 to 8 years in product marketing, or an equivalent blend of product marketing with marketing analytics, marketing or data ops, sales engineering, analytics consulting, or product management on a data product.

• Category fluency in marketing data and measurement: attribution models, incrementality testing, MMM, data governance and taxonomy, warehouses and ETL/ELT - including where each is honestly weak.

• B2B SaaS sold to marketing or data buyers. Marketing analytics, martech, measurement, CDP, BI and data-infrastructure vendors are the reference profile.

• Proof you have shipped, not just documented: positioning that changed the website and the pitch, battlecards reps actually opened, a win/loss program that survived past its second quarter.

• Writing that survives contact with a skeptical technical buye

Technical Escalation & Issue Resolution
